title: Item Record
description: The Generator → Orchestrator contract (core design doc §5.3): one item template with full metadata, i18n fields, render props, and Stage 5 provenance. Templates are parameterized item models (§2.1–2.2); the Orchestrator never constructs mathematics, it only selects (§5.1).

template_version.description: Version of this template, covering the answer-relevant content; carried on every attempt event (§5.3). Presentation-layer edits that leave the mathematics untouched — adding a figure to a stem that already described it in words — reuse the version deliberately, so variant signatures and student seen-state survive the rebuild. To trace the exact bytes behind a given answer, use the attempt's bank_version with that bank manifest's per-template source_sha256.

bank_version.description: Version of the atomic bank build this record ships in (§3 Stage 5, §5.3). Banks are never patched in place.

graph_version.description: Version of the canonical skill graph this record was authored against (§5.3); mastery records carry the same stamp for migration correctness (student-model doc §8).

skill_ids.description: Canonical skills this item measures. An array because exam-context (Olympiad-style) templates deliberately span two nodes (§2.10).

question_type.description: The §2.7 type taxonomy. MCQ is the diagnostic workhorse; low-guess formats (numeric_entry, drag_and_drop, visual_counting) certify mastery (§2.3). Keep this enum in sync with attempt-event.schema.json's question_type — the served item's type is copied verbatim onto its attempt event.

cognitive_level.description: Cognitive demand of the item, e.g. "application" (§2.2). Word problems sit higher on the depth axis with cognitive_level: application (§1.2a).

difficulty.description: Continuous difficulty D ∈ [0,1] — the actual data model (§2.3). Empirical calibration (Stage 6 IRT/Elo) moves this value smoothly.

difficulty_prior.description: The E/M/H authoring label — a named band over the difficulty scalar, stored as difficulty_prior (§2.2–2.3). Authoring interface and UI label only, never the data model.

estimated_time_sec.description: Expected time on item; at ~1.5× this value the engine proactively offers hint 1 (§2.3).

accepted_answer_forms.description: Which answer forms are accepted, e.g. "simplest form only" (§2.2).

values.description: Explicit value set for string variables.

variables.description: Template parameters with types and domains (§2.2). Domains are small enough for exhaustive Stage 3 enumeration (§3).

constraints.description: Constraint expressions over variables, e.g. "gcd(b, d) == 1" (§2.2). Difficulty tiers are defined by swapping constraint sets (§2.3).

stem_i18n.description: The question stem, keyed by language (§2.8). Contains {{variable}} and localization slots; v1 ships English-only but the schema carries _i18n keys from day one.

localization_slots.description: Slot names the locale pack fills: names, currency, units, contexts (§1.5, §2.2), e.g. ["name1", "name2", "food"].

answer.description: Machine-checkable answer logic, evaluated symbolically by Stage 3, e.g. "simplify((a*d + c*b) / (b*d))" (§2.2).

expr.description: Distractor expression, evaluated symbolically; any variant where it collides with the answer is dropped (§3 Stage 3).

misconception_id.description: Registry tag this distractor is designed to expose (§2.4). Nullable: an untagged distractor is plausible but carries no diagnosis (§2.5).

only_if.description: Optional guard expression; the distractor is only constructible when this holds, e.g. "gcd(a*d + c*b, b*d) > 1" (§2.2). Firing is measured against firing opportunity (§2.5).

unsimplified.description: Marks distractors that are the unsimplified answer form (§2.2).

distractors.description: Tagged distractor set (§2.2). The full distractor set is stored with every served instance so distractor opportunity is reconstructible (§5.1). Stage 3 collision checking (§3 Stage 3) compares ordinary distractors to the answer and to each other by reduced rational value; an unsimplified: true distractor is compared by its literal, unreduced numerator/denominator split instead, since its designed purpose is a value that coincides with the answer while displaying differently — see tools/item_verify.py's module docstring for the full convention.

additionalProperties.description: Pedagogy-variant key → ordered step list. Keyed by variant (NCERT, CC, …) where mapped curricula teach different methods, with a "canonical" variant as the default when methods coincide (§2.2).

solution_steps_i18n.description: Structured solution steps, language-keyed per §2.8 and pedagogy-variant-keyed per §2.2. Ordered structure (not a text blob); powers step-level feedback and faded worked examples (§6.1).

hints_i18n.description: The hint ladder, keyed by language (§2.8), ordered from lightest to strongest nudge. Hints are evidence, not just help (§2.3).

figure.description: Structured visual stimulus: render data, not images and not prose. Optional — omit it on text-only templates. Every figure-dependent template declares one (diagram_required: true), and the stem keeps its text description alongside so text-only consumers, TTS, and accessibility are unaffected. Values are expressions over the same variables the stem uses, evaluated offline by Stage 5; the array carries genuinely distinct figures, while a kind that repeats one element takes a count expression instead.

tts.description: Whether audio is synthesized for this template from stem_i18n and hints (§2.9). No separate audio authoring.

context_tags.description: Surface contexts (money, sports, food, travel, games…) so the engine can rotate dressing without touching the math (§2.7).

exam_contexts.description: Rigor wrappers this template serves (§2.10), e.g. SCHOOL_EXAM, OLYMPIAD_IMO_L1.

generator_version.description: Version of the Stage 2 generator that drafted this template (§3 Stage 5).

reviewer.description: Stage 4 human reviewer who approved the batch (§3 Stage 5).

provenance.description: Full provenance per §3 Stage 5: any later problem can be traced and every sibling item from the same flawed template pulled in one operation.

expr.description: A template expression over declared variables, e.g. "n" or "30*h". Stage 3 pre-parses it and Stage 5 evaluates it per variant; it never reaches a served instance unevaluated.

figureSpec.description: One authored figure, discriminated by kind. Twelve kinds cover the Class 6 census (docs/plans/2026-08-03-001-figure-census.md). Values are expressions, not numbers — the figure is materialized offline alongside the stem.

bars.description: Bar heights are whole gridline counts, so a bar top always lands on a gridline.

key_expr.description: Value one whole symbol represents; constrained even wherever a row uses a half symbol.

half.description: Draws a trailing half-clipped symbol worth key/2.

bundles_expr.description: Groups of five: four verticals crossed by a diagonal.

loose_expr.description: Ungrouped strokes, always fewer than five.

min_expr.description: May be negative — the integer line is centred on zero.

divisions_expr.description: Sub-divisions per whole unit; 1 gives integer ticks only.

position_expr.description: Rational or negative positions are expected.

label_i18n.description: Omit on read-the-value items — labelling the queried point leaks the answer.

degrees_expr.description: May exceed 180 — the reflex context draws the major arc.

context.description: clock draws a numbered hour-marked face; protractor overlays both scales.

scale.description: Which protractor scale the item reads; protractor context only.

tilt_expr.description: Rotation off upright, so a right angle is not axis-aligned.

arm_length_expr.description: Set where arm length is the contrast the item tests.

count_expr.description: Repeats this angle count times at differing tilts (KTD9) rather than varying the figures array length.

construction.description: segment-as-diameter marks the segment, its endpoints, and the centre.

points_off_expr.description: Points inside or outside; exact placement is renderer layout freedom (R7).

count_expr.description: Counts are variables across this family, so elements are never a fixed list.

shape.description: regular-ngon takes its side count from sides_expr.

side.description: Zero-based side index; label only the sides the item gives, since some items turn on a side being unlabelled.

rotation_expr.description: Degrees applied to the drawn shape.

symmetry.description: Whether to draw symmetry axes or mark rotational order.

shape.description: The whole being divided. Stems say only "a shape", so the figure names it.

weight_expr.description: Relative size. Parts are deliberately unequal in two of the three part-whole items.

count_expr.description: How many identical parts this entry stands for; defaults to 1. Every part-whole stem varies its piece count by variable, so a statically-enumerated list would contradict the stem on most variants. Bank build expands this into one instance part per drawn piece, the way the array kind expands its rows.

parts.description: Authored as groups of identical pieces; the materialized instance carries one entry per drawn piece.

per_row_expr.description: Marks in row i, one-based; "i" builds a triangular pile, a constant builds a rectangle.

half_cells_expr.description: Diagonally half-filled cells; their arrangement is deterministic renderer layout freedom (R7).

start_expr.description: Deliberately non-zero on the items that test reading from an offset.

objects.description: Two abutting objects share a join whose position no variable pins; the renderer picks it deterministically (R7).
